subject: Key decommissioning & archival proof requirements - Acero Medical SIG follow-up
messages:
From: Julie Ramos <julie.ramos@aceromedical.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acero Security <security@aceromedical.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Key decommissioning & archival proof requirements - SIG follow-up

Connor — thanks for the quick demo last week. One of the outstanding items from our SIG review is how Redwood handles permanent key decommissioning for customer-managed keys (BYOK) and what proof we can collect for archival/forensic purposes. Specifically, our audit team needs: 

1) A documented runbook for decommissioning a tenant key in the HSM (including zeroization steps).
2) Sample audit logs that show the decommissioning event plus the notarized hash/manifest used to attest the archival object.
3) Evidence that wrapped key material was not retained plaintext in any storage during the process (S3 objects, snapshots, backups).
4) Chain-of-custody record for any physical media if keys are exported for escrow.

We'd like a single packet our auditors can ingest (PDF/CSV + checklist). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide these items for Acero's BYOK keys, and an estimated delivery date?

Thanks,
Julie Ramos
Director, IT Risk & Compliance
Acero Medical
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julie Ramos <julie.ramos@aceromedical.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Key decommissioning & archival proof requirements - SIG follow-up

Julie — appreciate the clarity. Short answer: yes, we can deliver a compliance packet for BYOK decommissioning. I want to scope your asks into two deliverables so our legal/security folks are aligned:

A) Operational artifact bundle (what your auditors usually consume):
  - Decommission runbook (step-by-step with command lines and expected outputs)
  - HSM event logs (sample redacted) showing the decommission transaction and zeroization completion timestamps
  - Archival manifest (SHA256 hashes of archived objects) and a note on notarization process
  - Short attestation letter from Redwood security describing controls applied during decommission

B) Optional chain-of-custody attachments if you require physical escrow:
  - Signed handoff form, serial numbers of media, and witness signatures
  - Transport and storage disposition notes

I'll loop in our security ops lead and legal to confirm exportability/format and to produce the artifacts. Can we target a 5-business-day window for the initial packet? If Acero needs notarization or third-party signing, that may add time — let me know.

I'll also attach a draft decommission plan for internal review.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0147
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Julie Ramos <julie.ramos@aceromedical.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Key decommissioning & archival proof requirements - SIG follow-up

Team — forwarding Acero's asks. Summary below; please prepare the artifacts and confirm what we can provide without a contract amendment. Julie asked for: runbook, sample logs, archival manifest (notarized hash), proof of non-retention of plaintext, and chain-of-custody for physical escrow (optional).

Key constraints to flag up-front:
- For customer-managed HSM keys we operate under a sealed-wrapping model; we never store plaintext key material post-creation. We need to confirm which of the HSM logs we can share (some entries include internal job-ids we redact).
- Archival objects will be S3 objects containing: encrypted key-wrapping metadata, manifest CSV, and notarization hash. We should provide the manifest and notarization record, not the raw wrapped key material.

Deliverables I want from you:
1) Finalized keystore_decommission_plan.xlsx (detailed steps + expected outputs + redaction rules)
2) HSM redacted log sample (hsm-audit-log-sample.txt) annotated with explanation of fields
3) Short attestation paragraph we can include in the packet (one page)
4) A checklist mapping each SIG/CIS/CAIQ question to the artifact we are providing

Please also estimate the time to produce notarized hashes (if required) and whether we need legal to sign an attestation. Julie, if you can confirm whether Acero will accept a Redwood notarization (HSM-produced hash + timestamp) or if they require an external notary, that will help.

Thanks — Connor
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Julie Ramos <julie.ramos@aceromedical.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jun 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Key decommissioning & archival proof requirements - SIG follow-up

Connor / Julie — attached are the artifacts requested. High level notes: 

1) keystore_decommission_plan.xlsx (attached) — this is our standard BYOK decommission runbook adapted for tenant-scoped keys. It includes: pre-checks, HSM export/zeroize commands, required operator roles, expected event ids, and the redaction policy for logs and manifests.

2) hsm-audit-log-sample.txt (attached) — redacted sample covering a decommission workflow. We replaced operator UUIDs with role tags (e.g., <HSM_OP_ROLE>) and redacted internal job ids. Each log line is annotated with the field glossary.

3) acero_SIG_questionnaire_v2.pdf (attached) — mapping table: SIG question -> Artifact file / section / page. This should speed auditor review.

4) Archival manifest process: we publish a manifest CSV (filename pattern: <tenant>-decom-manifest-YYYYMMDD.csv) which lists object names, object SHA256, and a Redwood HSM-generated notarization token (signed timestamp). We will provide the manifest CSV and the notarization token. We do not ship wrapped key material in the packet.

5) Chain-of-custody (physical escrow): if Acero requires export to physical media, we will produce a signed handoff record with serial numbers and witness signatures. Note that physical export requires a formal request and legal sign-off (adds ~7 business days).

Estimated delivery: initial packet (items 1-3 + manifest + notarization token) by Tue 2028-06-13 (5 business days). If Acero requires an external notary or physical escrow, add 7-10 business days.

Julie — does this timeline work? If so we'll package the PDF/CSV bundle and provide a short attestation signed by Redwood security.

—Grace O'Connor
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
Grace.O@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0214

Attachments referenced: keystore_decommission_plan.xlsx (workflow, redaction rules), hsm-audit-log-sample.txt (annotated), acero_SIG_questionnaire_v2.pdf (mapping)
